title: Bangladesh Rules Out PM Tarique Rahman's Attendance at Delhi BRICS Summit
excerpt: Dhaka says the BRICS invitation was extended to the BIMSTEC chair, not to Prime Minister Tarique Rahman personally, and insists his first India visit cannot be a multilateral one.
body:
• Bangladesh on Wednesday ruled out Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's attendance at the BRICS Summit in New Delhi on September 12–13, saying he was not invited in his capacity as prime minister.
  • The invitation was extended to Bangladesh as the current chair of BIMSTEC — a distinction Dhaka insists on, with the state foreign minister asking, "How shall we go? Has anyone from the Bangladesh government been invited?"
  • Dhaka says Rahman's first visit to India cannot be a multilateral one, and that it is working on a bilateral visit when the timing is conducive.
  • India's foreign ministry said it had no fresh update on the leader's participation, while reaffirming its commitment to advancing bilateral ties.

Bangladesh on Wednesday ruled out Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's attendance at the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, declaring that the invitation was extended to him as the chair of the regional grouping BIMSTEC — not as the prime minister of Bangladesh.

"How shall we go? Has anyone from the Bangladesh government been invited? Our prime minister was not invited. Who told you that our prime minister was invited? The BIMSTEC chair was invited. Then why are you asking this question?" State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir told reporters at the Foreign Service Academy in Dhaka, according to the BNP media cell. He added that Prime Minister Rahman's first visit to India cannot be a multilateral visit.

Context and Background

Bangladesh assumed the chairmanship of the Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation — BIMSTEC, comprising Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka, and Thailand — in April 2025 for a two-year term. India, hosting this year's BRICS Summit, invited the BIMSTEC chair to attend the summit's outreach session, a practice hosts use to draw regional partners into the gathering.

"Then why are you asking this question?" State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir told reporters at the Foreign Service Academy in Dhaka, according to the BNP media cell."

Dhaka has received two separate invitations from India, officials have said: one from Prime Minister Narendra Modi for a bilateral visit — reportedly extended in February, after Rahman took office — and another for the BIMSTEC chairperson to attend the BRICS Summit. State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam said on July 23 that the foreign ministry had received the invitation from the Indian side and forwarded it to the Prime Minister's Office.

Foreign Minister Khalilur Rahman had earlier urged the media to understand the difference between the two invitations, noting the BRICS invitation was "addressed to the chairperson of BIMSTEC," not to the prime minister personally.

A Careful Balancing Act

Kobir said the government is working to arrange a bilateral visit to India when the timing is conducive — signaling that Dhaka wants Rahman's first India trip to be a standalone engagement, not a walk-on role at a multilateral summit. The distinction matters because the BRICS invitation generated discussion over whether New Delhi had extended a fresh personal invitation to Rahman.

The caution reflects the delicate state of the relationship. Rahman has reportedly been reluctant to visit India while former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina remains on Indian soil, amid concerns about a domestic backlash, the Times of India reported earlier. Bangladesh also aspires to BRICS membership and has already received support from China and Russia, with both President Xi Jinping and President Vladimir Putin expected to attend the summit. Rahman has recently visited Malaysia and China and plans trips to Japan and the United States for the UN General Assembly later this year.

India's Response

India's Ministry of External Affairs said on Tuesday it had no fresh update on the Bangladesh leader's participation. "I don't have any update," spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said at a media briefing, leaving attendance unconfirmed.

Jaiswal reaffirmed India's commitment to advancing bilateral ties, characterizing a recent high-level engagement in Dhaka as constructive. Indian High Commissioner to Bangladesh Dinesh Trivedi paid a courtesy call on Bangladesh President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir on Tuesday, where they discussed strengthening bilateral relations "with a people-centric approach," covering areas including security cooperation, according to the MEA. The president emphasized resolving pending issues between the two countries through discussion.

Diaspora Angle

The India-Bangladesh relationship is watched closely by the large Bangladeshi diaspora — in India, the United States, and the Gulf — as well as Indian-Americans with ties across the border. Every public signal about the first Rahman-Modi meeting sets expectations for trade, border, and water-sharing issues that affect millions of families on both sides.

What's Next

The 18th BRICS Summit opens Saturday at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi, with India chairing the grouping for 2026 under the theme "Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability." The real test for Dhaka-Delhi ties comes after: whether the two sides can lock in dates for Rahman's bilateral visit — the engagement both capitals say they want, on terms both can accept.
